flash.message: {name} is a flash card — the learner grades it, not the app.
flash.fix: Make it a question the app grades: one, many, truefalse, match, order, number, gap, or text with every accepted answer.

noTower.message: {name} belongs to no tower (its “about” names no tower).
noTower.fix: Set “about” to the tower the question tests — every question belongs to a tower.

untaught.message: {name}: no slide teaches its tower {tower} or a tower it requires.
untaught.fix: Teach it on a slide of the tower (linked to the tower) or of a required tower, link the slide in “explain”, or delete the question.
untaught.scenes: (This base has presentation stories: their scenes are not visible to this check — if a scene teaches it, all is well.)

message.one: {name}: {count} of {total} options has no feedback sentence.
message.other: {name}: {count} of {total} options have no feedback sentence.

noFeedback.fix: Give every option its own sentence (“feedback”, one per option, same order) saying why it is right or wrong.

noCore.fix: Mark the 1–2 questions that test the heart of the tower with "core": true.

fewVote.message: Tower {name}: {count} question(s) ready for a class vote — at least {min} are needed.
fewVote.fix: Add questions of the form “one” with {options} options where every wrong option is a named thinking error (“tags”).

longestCorrect.message: Tower {name}: the correct option is the longest in {count} of {total} choice questions ({share} %).
longestCorrect.fix: Make the wrong options as long and credible as the right one — the right one may be the longest in at most 3 of 10 questions.

positions.message: Tower {name}: the correct option is at position {position} in {count} of {total} choice questions.
positions.fix: Spread the position of the correct option evenly over the questions.

long.message: {name}: {count} words — a slide carries one thought, at most about {max} words.
long.fix: Split it into two slides, or cut what the learner does not need here.

severalTowers.message: Path {name} leads through {count} towers ({list}) — a path leads to one tower.
severalTowers.fix: Split it into one path per tower, or end it at an outer fork whose branches lead to the towers.

slidesInRow.message: Path {name}: {count} slides in a row at {step} (at most {max}).
slidesInRow.fix: At most {max} slides in a row: after one or two slides, a question about exactly them.

questionsInRow.message: Path {name}: {count} questions in a row at {step} (at most {max} outside the closing block).
questionsInRow.fix: At most {max} questions in a row: put the slide that prepares a question right before it, or move them to the closing block.

longClosing.message: Path {name}: the closing block has {count} questions (2–{max}).
longClosing.fix: Keep 2–{max} questions that connect the steps; the tower asks the rest in its run and in reviews.

noQuestions.message: Path {name} shows slides but asks nothing.
noQuestions.fix: Alternate: one or two slides, then a question about exactly them.

ticket.message: Path {name} requires {list} before it starts — more than its first tower {tower} requires.
ticket.fix: A ticket requires only what the first tower of the line requires: move the requirement to the tower (“Wymaga”) or let the line start at a later tower.

labelLong.message: Path {name}: the fork option {label} has {count} characters (at most {max}).
labelLong.fix: Give the option a short line name of at most {max} characters; say more in its hint.

hintLong.message: Path {name}: the hint of {label} has {count} characters (at most {max}).
hintLong.fix: Shorten the hint to at most {max} characters.

message.one: {name}: the error tag {list} has no help in the path {path} that asks it.
message.other: {name}: the error tags {list} have no help in the path {path} that asks it.

noHelp.fix: Lead each named error to the slide that resolves it: onWrong.byTag (or an edge wrong:<tag>) at the question step.

nearDuplicate.message: The error tags {a} ({ca}×) and {b} ({cb}×) look like the same error written differently.
nearDuplicate.fix: Use one spelling for one thinking error and retag the options.

message.one: {count} error tag occurs in one option only: {list}.
message.other: {count} error tags occur in one option only: {list}.

usedOnce.fix: A tag names a typical thinking error that recurs — check whether an existing tag fits.

usedOnce.message: The tag {name} selects one tower only ({tower}).
usedOnce.fix: Reuse an existing tag, or drop a tag that selects a single tower.

nearDuplicate.message: The tags {a} and {b} look like the same word in another form.
nearDuplicate.fix: Keep one of them and retag the towers.

standard.message: Conquest levels: {now}. Recommended for every world: two levels — 75 % with any attempts, 90 % with one correction, paths open from level 1.
standard.fix: Ask the owner whether to switch to the two-level standard (levelsSetup) — do not switch silently.

open.fix: Read them (get_feedback), fix what they report, and resolve them in the import file: "feedback": [{"id": …, "state": "done", "note": …}].

preview.fix: Fix the path in the flow editor or in the import file (guide-stories); the import preview says the same.

slides.fix: Fix the text of the slide (guide-stories, slides and text).

landscape.fix: Fix the order of learning or the view (guide-world-map).

worlds.fix: Fix the link into the other world ("@@handle:…", with "external": true in a reference field).

map.fix: See guide-world-map: towers, prerequisites and paths.

panel.title: World check
panel.lede: What the world still needs according to the guide for good worlds — a to-do list, nothing is blocked. The same list reaches AI assistants (get_world_checks).
panel.none: The world check finds nothing to do.

linear.message: The world reads like a text: {count} of {total} towers stand in one line, each with at most one tower directly before and one after it.
linear.fix: Keep the order of the source as one dimension, but add others over the same towers: an overview with scenes and details under it, threads that follow a main character or a topic across scenes (question paths, tags), towers that join several scenes. See guide-good-world 1.2a.

oneLevel.message: All {total} towers stand on one level of detail: no overview with parts under it, no blocks, no deepening paths.
oneLevel.fix: Build levels: an overview tower (several towers build on it), blocks ("part": "up") for a large part, and deeper paths through detour (optional: true) — one, two, three or more levels.

noThreads.message: The {total} towers can only be met in the order of the source: no question path through several towers, no tag that gathers towers from different parts, no tower that joins several scenes.
noThreads.fix: Add orders across the source: a question path that follows a main character, a tag for a topic or a person, a tower that compares the first and the last scene. The towers stay the same; only the way through them is new.

dimensions.message: Dimensions of the world ({total} towers, {chain} in a chain): levels of detail {levels} (blocks {blocks}, deepened towers {deepenings}, overviews {overviews}); threads across the order: question paths {paths}, tags across parts {tags}, joining towers {joins}.
dimensions.fix: A good world uses several dimensions over the same towers: the order of the source, levels of detail, and threads (a character, a topic) — guide-good-world 1.2a.
